scores.evidence: Postgres sequences leave gaps when a transaction rolls back, and several tax authorities object to gaps
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate throughout, including subtle areas (Stripe idempotency key expiry, webhook retry window, RLS ownership bypass, SET LOCAL with PgBouncer, partitioned-table unique indexes), with no material error found.

scores.evidence: If you meant the billing part of your own SaaS product, see the Build-vs-buy flip in §2. It changes most of this plan.
scores.rationale: It resolves the request's central ambiguity explicitly, covers every core billing capability, and defers non-essentials with stated triggers in §7.

scores.evidence: Each module owns its tables and talks to others through interfaces and outbox events.
scores.rationale: Decisions made once (tenant-first keys, Money type, CP for money, outbox) are honored consistently in every later phase with no internal contradictions.

scores.evidence: forces timeouts after Stripe has already succeeded; kills workers mid-charge; replays every webhook three times, out of order
scores.rationale: Each phase has exit checks aimed at its specific failure risks, risky guesses are measured early (Phase 2 ledger load test replaces the §2 guess), and validation continues in production via canaries and reconciliation.

scores.evidence: Move to TigerBeetle or Modern Treasury Ledgers when sustained postings near the ceiling measured in Phase 2 (initial guess about 5k/s)
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit, numbers are labeled as guesses to be measured, and every decision carries a revisit trigger stating what would change the design and when.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: A silent wrong charge at scale... a retried billing run charges cards twice across many tenants
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates, out-of-order webhooks, timeout-after-success, SSRF, enumeration via 404-vs-403, ledger corruption detection, provider outages and billing-run anomaly stops, each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: page if a due period goes uninvoiced for more than 2 h, since that is revenue lost silently
scores.rationale: Deployment with automatic rollback, additive migrations with CI enforcement, domain-meaningful alerts, break-glass access, restore drills and a staff console are all concrete and sized to a small team on managed AWS.

scores.evidence: Infrastructure is managed AWS (RDS, ECS Fargate, KMS), not self-run Kubernetes or Postgres.
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy and cost-deferring triggers are the implicit cost reasoning, but there are no run-cost or engineering-effort estimates, no vendor fee discussion, and no analysis of how costs grow with usage.

scores.evidence: Because every key starts with tenant_id, the move is a data copy, not a rewrite.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (funds flow, money representation, tenancy, public contract, ledger) get the most scrutiny and early validation, while reversible ones are explicitly flagged flexible behind interfaces and flags.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith. One repo, one image, one Postgres.
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable design (Postgres job queue instead of Kafka, one cell, deferred Temporal/ClickHouse/multi-region) with explicit growth triggers, while omitting no billing essential.

scores.evidence: An internal canary tenant sends POST /v1/invoices with an Idempotency-Key header and this body
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: Phase 0 is a concrete end-to-end slice, phases are dependency-ordered with reasons, every phase has checkable exit criteria, and revisit triggers say how to adapt.

checklist.evidence: Integers in the currency's smallest unit (bigint) plus the ISO-4217 code... Rounding happens once per line, half-up
Updates and deletes are blocked, and corrections are reversing entries. Finalized invoices never change; corrections are credit notes.
Exactly one PaymentIntent per invoice, created with the invoice ID as its idempotency key and saved before it's confirmed.
Card details are collected only through Stripe Elements and SetupIntents, so we hold pm_… tokens and never a card number.
RLS is forced on every tenant table, and the app role has no BYPASSRLS... An isolation test suite runs in CI and nightly in prod
duplicates are dropped by (tenant_id, event_id) for 35 days... official numbers are recomputed from raw events at period close
a price can't change once it's been used, so editing creates a new version... Month-end start dates clamp: Jan 31, then Feb 28
take the next gap-free invoice number from a per-tenant, per-series counter row... if the provider is down, finalization waits and never guesses the tax
retry schedules per tenant based on decline codes, never retrying hard declines; moves subscriptions from past_due to unpaid or canceled
Daily PSP reconciliation matches every Stripe balance transaction to a ledger posting by PSP ID, and anything unmatched in either direction pages someone.
An entitlements API: build when tenants ask to gate product features by plan in real time.
Build the core: catalog, subscriptions, metering, rating, invoicing and the ledger. That is the product. Buy the rest: payments (Stripe Connect)

traps.evidence: Integers in the currency's smallest unit (bigint) plus the ISO-4217 code... All arithmetic goes through one Money type.
a trigger rejects changes to financial columns once an invoice is finalized... corrections are credit notes
verify the signature... store the raw event, unique on its event ID... handle duplicates and out-of-order events by re-fetching the object
we hold pm_… tokens and never a card number. PCI scope is limited to card tokens.
CI rejects any migration that adds a table without RLS or without tenant_id-first keys.

note: An exceptionally strong, technically precise billing architecture that avoids every domain trap, with explicit assumptions, risk-first validation and reversibility reasoning; its only notable weakness is the absence of explicit money/effort cost estimates.
